title: Canonical chat history and authority are not contracted
path: New conversation -> Hermes inherited session/profile -> unselected history or tools enter reply.
fix: Define canonical transcript/session mapping; R1 tools and automatic memory closed; R2 memory only through scoped gateway; bind model/profile versions.
expected: No implicit old-space context or broadened tools; original run retains its binding.

title: Runtime attach, authentication and ownership handshake is incomplete
path: Double launch -> each discovers a different endpoint or starts a new root -> split state; Quit may stop a shared runtime.
fix: Specify stable app-data root, instance/API/schema descriptor, authenticated attach/start lease and owned-versus-shared shutdown. A port or PID alone is not proof of identity.
expected: Exactly one owner of the selected data root; authenticated attach; no unrelated service termination.

title: Crash-safe chat acceptance and dispatch are only an intention
path: Submit -> durable acceptance -> lost acknowledgement -> new request ID -> duplicate inference/cost.
fix: Persist request hash, user message and run identity atomically; reserve dispatch before calling Hermes; reconnect observes; explicit read retry creates a separate bounded attempt.
expected: One local dispatch per attempt; changed input rejected; uncertainty never masquerades as unsent.

title: Stream ordering, terminal precedence and cursor recovery are undefined
path: Cancel confirmed -> late completion; switch view -> old delta; reconnect -> duplicate final.
fix: Define scoped event envelope, monotone sequence, snapshot fallback, terminal transition rules and bounded buffering. Separate stop requested from stop confirmed.
expected: No wrong-view output, duplicate final or cancelled-run resurrection; recover by snapshot without resubmission.

title: UI data-fetch and action retry policies are not separated
path: IPC times out after applying an action -> data library reconnect/retry resubmits operation.
fix: Use read observation only in retryable queries; explicit idempotent command handlers with canonical request IDs; uncertain writes only reconcile. No generic replay on reconnect.
expected: No automatic effect replay; observation and commands have distinct policies.

title: Data schema/version and supported downgrade rules need a first-release floor
path: R2 changes SQLite -> user returns to R1 -> old app silently writes new schema.
fix: Initialize schema/API version negotiation in R1; later migrations need exclusive ownership, recovery points and supported downgrade rules; unsupported writer refuses.
expected: No silent incompatible write or concurrent live-store copy; a defined recovery path exists.

title: Untrusted Markdown and source-opening policy lacks concrete tests
path: Model/source output contains active HTML, tracking images, dangerous URI or forged local-file link.
fix: Specify sanitization and CSP; remote content cannot call IPC; external images require permitted loading; citation resolver uses scoped resource IDs; sender/frame and URL checks are authoritative.
expected: No script, unexpected network request or arbitrary OS/file operation; source grants enforced.

title: Local read consent and provider disclosure consent are not the same grant
path: User selects a private document for local reading -> its contents go to a remote model without a defined disclosure policy.
fix: Define first-run provider disclosure and per-data-class egress; bind provider/model policy to run; attachments obey both read and disclosure permissions.
expected: No prohibited upload; user sees actual provider and compatible choices without repeated meaningless prompts.

title: Forget is not closed over transcripts, caches, pending runs and restore
path: Retract/forget fact -> new context includes old transcript or restored cached source -> fact returns as current.
fix: Define correction/retraction versus erasure; tombstones, derived-context invalidation, pending-run handling, exports/backups and fresh-session behaviour; add an explicit forget path.
expected: No current-use resurrection within the declared deletion scope; retained history/backup limits are explicit.

title: Concurrent review and changing context need an atomic decision contract
path: Two windows approve/reject the same proposal; editor changes content; account switches before dispatch.
fix: Bind exact resource/account generation, payload, version and expiry; consume approval with backend compare-and-set; pending edit invalidates old digest; final dispatch revalidates.
expected: At most one accepted decision; exact original target only; no stale authority.

title: Connection expiry, reconnect and disconnect lifecycle is underspecified
path: Testing-mode token expires -> scheduled read fails -> UI still says connected; reconnect selects a different account.
fix: Separate configured/authenticated/qualified/authorized status; detect scope loss, expiration and account identity changes; disconnect revokes grants and suppresses late delivery; distinguish disable, remove credential and provider revocation.
expected: Actionable re-consent state; no account substitution or late revoked data delivery.

title: Persisted workflows cannot reuse process-local short-lived grants after restart
path: Save a five-minute read grant or two-minute context ticket in a template -> scheduled run days later/restart.
fix: Templates bind resource intentions/versioned standing authorization, not temporary tickets; mint fresh task grants only within valid standing scope; revalidate evidence at use.
expected: Expired references are not revived; fresh narrowly authorized grants/context or an explicit blocked state.

title: Local task and Google task synchronization rules are absent
path: Google needsAction passes through an object documented as pending/completed, while etag/updated are omitted; later local/provider edits have no defined normalization or conflict basis.
fix: Define raw versus canonical task status, local/provider IDs, retained provider versions, source authority, conflict UI and complete/delete tombstones. If no sync, label an explicit import/draft.
expected: No silent overwrite, duplicate task or completed-task resurrection; conflicts remain reviewable.

title: A generic receipt pattern does not qualify every external write
path: Provider accepts a send/event change -> acknowledgement lost -> verify using an unrelated matching item.
fix: Per operation define provider IDs/versions, attribution, verified/failed/unknown states and read-only reconciliation; transport success alone is insufficient.
expected: Completion is attributed to the reviewed operation; absent/unattributed remains unknown without automatic retry.

title: Typed dependency outputs, version pinning and evidence expiry need exact rules
path: Template edited during run; malformed step output feeds synthesis; old evidence silently reused.
fix: Freeze template/capability versions per run; schema-validate each edge; reject missing outputs/cycles; track observed-at/source versions and refresh or withhold stale context.
expected: Active run is not retargeted; bad/stale output does not become trusted downstream input.

title: Cancellation, queue fairness and aggregate budgets are not defined for a run tree
path: Each child meets its own limit but total calls grow; background work starves chat; cancel releases capacity while upstream work continues.
fix: Bound total steps/calls/tokens/time/concurrency across descendants; interactive versus background queue policy; cancel propagation and retained receipts; unknown cost stays unknown.
expected: UI remains responsive; bounded queue/budgets; no child continues with newly revoked rights; cancellation limits visible.

title: DST gaps/folds, overlap and missed-run policies remain choices rather than contracts
path: A local time occurs twice or never; laptop sleeps through several occurrences; prior run is still active.
fix: Store IANA zone and explicit gap/fold/fixed-versus-follow-device policy; default no overlap; bounded missed-run/coalescing; occurrence identity and clock-change handling.
expected: Documented number/timing of runs; no duplicate occurrence or unbounded backlog.

title: Cron dispatch and application Quit must preserve the same authority
path: Hermes scheduler remains alive after UI Quit or dispatches a raw prompt with inherited tools.
fix: Qualify a fixed trusted scheduling entry through Wayfinder; background grants explicit; Quit/stop-all semantics cover Wayfinder jobs without killing unrelated Hermes tasks. No unrestricted fallback.
expected: No unauthorized background effect; failures stay blocked; shared host is not indiscriminately stopped.

title: Skill/plugin update and rollback can change permissions under a saved workflow
path: Approved workflow resolves a newly installed skill/tool version; rollback is mistaken for undoing prior effects.
fix: Pin versions and required rights; review manifest changes; disable/revoke invalidates relevant pending authority; rollback changes future configuration only, not external history.
expected: No inherited new rights or silent version substitution; previous effects retain their receipts.

title: Memory quality is not established by storage fixtures and one model run
path: Fixture embeddings pass but paraphrased/historical/conflicting retrieval chooses wrong evidence.
fix: Retain explicit held-out current/history/conflict/missing cases, source fidelity and disclosure checks; qualify neural path separately from deterministic fixtures; thresholds before judging release.
expected: Correct scoped evidence or explicit uncertainty; no invented current fact; report actual evaluation tier.

title: Google task due dates are not timed reminders
source: PLAN.md:118; Google Tasks resource reference; model-results.json:date_boundaries
path: Display due date via generic UTC-to-local timestamp conversion -> preceding day; promise a 10:00 task reminder the API cannot retain.
fix: Separate due_date, local reminder time and scheduled occurrence; preserve date-only semantics; unsupported timed behaviour is explicit.
expected: Date stays the intended calendar date; timing uses a separately qualified scheduler/calendar operation.

title: Old citations may point to expired grants or changed resources
path: Reopen an old chat -> source grant expired or file changed -> open link silently reads the new source.
fix: Separate historical retained evidence from current source access; show observed version and unavailable state; request a fresh selection/grant where needed.
expected: No unauthorized refresh or claim that changed content is the original evidence.

title: Event sequence and identifier types can be rounded by JavaScript
path: A large sequence, timestamp or ID crosses JSON as Number -> duplicate/order checks compare rounded values.
fix: Use opaque strings and decimal-string large counters; explicit TypeScript decoding and schema tests; never turn IDs into Number for routing.
expected: Exact identity/order preserved without coercion or serialization failure.

title: Attachment limits, parser truncation and temporary-copy retention need user behaviour
path: Oversize/unsupported/renamed/locked file appears attached; partial parsing shown as complete; remote copies outlive local grant.
fix: Validate selected file and disclose actual support/limits; retain source hash; show partial extraction; define temporary/sandbox copy cleanup and revoke semantics.
expected: Actionable selection error or explicit partial result; no silent format fallback or retention claim.

title: A single runtime-ready label hides different dependency and cold-start failures
path: Hermes is ready but FalkorDB/model cache is unavailable; first embedding download looks like a frozen app.
fix: Component-level health/startup states and dependency prerequisites; cold-cache/offline/disk-full paths; no automatic privileged restart/install to hide failure.
expected: Honest usable or blocked state; progress is accurate; other projects/services remain untouched.

title: Composer focus outline overrides its own focus-visible design
path: Keyboard reaches composer -> outline:none!important defeats declared focus style.
fix: Remove the conflicting rule or provide a clear focus-within indicator; verify in real keyboard/high-contrast tests. Do not infer screen-reader quality from the fake DOM.
expected: Visible focus and readable composer; no focus trap or clipped controls.

title: Feature gating applies to navigation but not inspector or sample conversation
path: Choose R1 -> Google plan/review remain; choose R2 -> Google calendar/tasks request is shown.
fix: Use the same release/capability manifest for all surfaces, examples, actions and inspector tabs. Keep unavailable capabilities inaccessible except an explicitly labelled roadmap.
expected: No R3 task approval/Google data in earlier releases; appropriate phase-specific examples.

title: Narrow layout hides the sidebar with no reopening path
path: Below 760px -> Tasks/Memory/Workflows sidebar disappears -> rail offers no drawer opener.
fix: Implement accessible navigation drawer with open/close, focus and Escape; preserve route and selected context.
expected: All enabled destinations remain reachable; no keyboard or pointer dead end.

title: Wide inspector does not obey the show/hide toggle
path: At desktop width toggle show-inspector -> inspector stays visible because only the narrow media rule reacts.
fix: Use one actual visibility state for grid/sheet; update control label and aria-expanded; preserve user preference deliberately.
expected: Inspector opens and closes correctly at all supported widths without losing review state.

title: IME Enter is treated as submit
path: Confirm composed text with Enter -> handler prevents default and runs submit path.
fix: Ignore submit during composition (and relevant platform key composition states); keep multiline and screen-reader input intact.
expected: Composition is not submitted; intended newline/submit behaviours remain correct.

title: Optional subreleases and optional W37 lack machine-readable gate status
path: Read-only R3a or deferred native testing appears blocked by an unqualified write/native case.
fix: Add required/optional, capability precondition, release variant, justified N/A, evidence tier and owner fields; no blanket N/A for mandatory scope.
expected: Advertised scope is testable and honest; optional work does not fake-pass or indefinitely block unrelated accepted features.

title: Web research and knowledge/notes roles have no concrete delivery slice
path: User asks for web research or notes promised by worker coverage -> no release defines its connector and test.
fix: Assign a named optional read-only research/knowledge slice with actual Tavily/notes qualification, disclosure limits and source verification; or explicitly defer it in the release manifest.
expected: Available operation is real and sourced; unshipped capabilities are clearly unavailable.

title: The full W01-W47 to concrete runtime binding catalogue is not reconciled
path: User enables a numbered role -> overlapping named registry entries resolve differently or cannot resolve.
fix: One versioned ID/alias/contract/owner/binding inventory; every planned role mapped, deferred or unsupported; never invent a prompt to fill a missing mapping.
expected: No duplicate worker or false Available status; missing contracts remain explicit.

title: Transcript, drafts, run artifacts and logs have different deletion/storage pressure behaviour
path: Clear an artifact -> copies persist in worker jobs/transcripts; storage fills while app promises a completed save.
fix: Define retention and purge scope per record type, safe redacted export and disk-full handling; delete wording matches actual copies and backup limits.
expected: No false erasure/save; clear recovery and independent lifecycle controls.

title: Quick-window position, hotkey conflicts and close/reopen recovery are untested
path: Undock monitor or change DPI -> quick window restored offscreen; global hotkey conflicts silently.
fix: Clamp saved bounds to available displays, provide visible restore/reset entry, handle hotkey registration failure and document close/minimize/tray/Quit separately.
expected: Window remains recoverable; no silent hijack or uncloseable always-on-top state.

title: Build/runtime version matrix is not resolved for the selected host
path: Current upstream host requires newer build tooling than the installed Node; copied UI code fails before the R1 package exists.
fix: Record pinned host/SDK/Node/Python/Electron/API compatibility and license basis; resolve in the host spike without upgrading the active Hermes runtime by assumption.
expected: Reproducible supported build or explicit no-go; no silent main-runtime upgrade or permissions fallback.
